title: Ham, cheddar and Bramley breakfast loaf

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Flour, eggs, milk, oil, cooked ham, cheddar, mustard and a Bramley are all ordinary cupboard and fridge food.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a loaf tin, bowl, jug and grater, and the technique is a simple quick-bread mix.

works.reason: The flour, egg, milk and oil ratio with a grated Bramley suits a 900g tin, and 50 minutes at 190°C (170°C fan) is right for a savoury loaf.

honest_times.reason: The printed 60 cook minutes do not match the 50-minute bake in the steps, and the time_note is blank, so nothing tells a reader that a breakfast needing 70-plus minutes and cooling before slicing must be made ahead.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the sage, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm baked loaf suits December, and the grated Bramley gives the loaf its moisture and sharpness rather than sitting on top as a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: Ham, cheese, eggs and apple make it a filling breakfast of real food, not just starch.
